then.text: Best sandbar crew in the Sound, thanks to you. The rays have been waving at your boat. I think. It's hard to tell with rays.
You've shown my rival who's boss. And the rays like you. That's the only vote I've ever cared about.
Take this: a bracelet of silver thatch, woven by my aunt. The thatch palm's the national tree, and she's the national treasure.

else.text: Last job: my rival diver, Nasir, has been telling the tourists he's the rays' favourite. He's pacing the shore of the Sound. Put him right.

then.text: A raylette! Look at the little flaps. That's a stingray in the making.

else.text: The rays are happy. Now catch one yourself, a raylette, and show me. They live in the shallows of the Sound. Gently does it.
The squid goes to the stingray on the sandbar. Out through the shallows, beyond the boats. Don't drop it. They'll never forgive you.
Old Fisher on the quay has a bucket of squid with your name on it. Fetch it, then feed the stingray on the sandbar.
Welcome aboard. Stingray City is a sandbar in the North Sound. Southern stingrays started gathering there because the fishermen cleaned their catch on it. Now the tourists feed them squid.
The rays know my boat engine from a mile off. Do me a favour: bring squid out to the sandbar, then catch a raylette to show me, and see off my rival. Old Fisher has the squid.

then.text: Squid delivered. Now go and put it in the stingray's face. In a nice way.

else.text: Mac sent you? Here, a bucket of squid. Cleaned, chopped and slightly smelly. They love it.
Fish rundown, that's what my mother made. Fish simmered in coconut milk till it falls apart. Cayman food is about patience and coconut.

then.text: The stingray glides between your ankles and flaps off, content.

else.text: You hold out the squid. A southern stingray as wide as a doormat slides up, takes it, and drapes itself against your leg. It is velvet. It is very gentle. It is also looking for more squid.
A stingray ripples past, hopeful. It's wondering if you have squid. You do not.

cay_banker.text: The Cayman dollar is worth more than the US dollar, about 1.20 to one. It's pegged. It does not move. Neither do I, after lunch.
George Town's a financial centre. We have the weather and the paperwork.

cay_cook.text: Conch fritters! Chopped queen conch in a spiced batter, fried till golden. Dip in the sauce. Not the other sauce. The orange one.
Cassava heavy cake is the real Cayman treat. Grated cassava, sugar, coconut. It lives up to its name.

cay_ranger2.text: The blue iguanas weren't blue when they were hatched; they get bluer as they get older and, in the breeding season, the males go properly sapphire.
Twenty years ago there were maybe a couple of dozen left in the wild. We have more now. Not enough, but more. Keep your dog on a lead and a wide berth round the road.

cay_turtle.text: The Turtle Centre breeds green turtles and releases some every year. It started because people ate turtles for centuries, which is why Columbus called the islands Las Tortugas.
A green turtle can live for decades and cross oceans to come back to the very beach it hatched on. I can't find my car keys.

cay_pirate.text: Pirates Week is in November! There's a mock invasion, a parade, and everybody is a pirate. You're a pirate too. You just don't know it yet.

cay_home.text: Heading back to Brize Norton? The RAF flight leaves Owen Roberts when the pilot's finished his coffee.
Head home to RAF Brize Norton?

then.text: Right-o. Seatbelts, sunscreen and stowaway iguanas are all checked.

else.text: Take your time. We'll be here.
